title: Search Autocomplete (Typeahead): Complete Architecture
description: Design a real-time search typeahead system (Google / Amazon scale) with prefix Tries, Top-K caching at nodes, offline aggregation, and sub-30ms latency.

data.text: Design a real-time search autocomplete (typeahead) system like Google Suggest or Amazon Search Bar. As a user types each keystroke into the search input, the system instantly suggests the top 5 to 10 most relevant, high-frequency completions. The system must serve 5+ billion queries daily at hundreds of thousands of queries per second, achieve strict sub-30ms P99 latency globally, filter offensive queries, and continuously update popularity scores as new search trends emerge.

terms.definition: A tree data structure where each node represents a character; all descendant nodes share a common prefix defined by their path from the root.
Storing the top 5-10 most popular completed queries directly at every Trie node, reducing lookup time from O(subtree size) to O(prefix length).
Delaying API network calls until the user pauses typing for 150-300ms, eliminating redundant requests during rapid typing.
Partitioning prefixes across Trie server shards using consistent hashing to balance memory and query load evenly across nodes.
An offline Spark/MapReduce batch job that aggregates query frequencies over rolling 7-day windows and publishes serialized Trie snapshots.

data.title: Functional Requirements
items: Prefix Matching: Return top 5-10 relevant query suggestions matching the typed prefix string
Popularity Ranking: Rank suggestions based on historical query frequency, recency, and trending weight
Fuzzy & Typo Tolerance: Suggest corrections for common spelling errors and transpositions
Content Moderation: Filter hate speech, explicit content, and sensitive terms via a denylist filter
Personalization: Blend globally trending suggestions with user personal recent search history

data.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items: Ultra-Low Latency: Sub-30ms P99 response time end-to-end (every keystroke must feel instant)
Extreme High Availability: 99.999% uptime for the autocomplete read path
Scale: 5+ billion autocomplete queries/day (~60,000 QPS average, 250,000 QPS peak)
Memory Efficiency: Trie structures must be optimized and compacted to fit in distributed server RAM
Scalable Ingestion: Stream and aggregate billions of raw search click logs without slowing read traffic

data.text: The architecture cleanly separates the real-time Read Path (Client Debounce, Edge CDN, Autocomplete Gateway, and Sharded In-Memory Trie Cache) from the offline Analytics & Indexing Pipeline (Kafka, Spark Aggregator, and Trie Builder).

data.text: With Top-K suggestions pre-stored at each node, looking up a prefix requires only traversing down the tree to the prefix node (O(L) where L is prefix length) and returning the list immediately.

faqs.question: Why store Top-K suggestions directly at every Trie node instead of searching on the fly?
faqs.answer: In a standard Trie, once you reach the node for prefix "ca", you must traverse all thousands of sub-branches ("car", "cat", "card", etc.) to identify the 5 highest-frequency queries, taking 50-100ms. By caching the top 5 queries directly at the "ca" node, the search completes the instant the prefix node is reached in O(length) time (<2ms).

faqs.question: How much memory does a Trie with Top-K caching consume for 100M queries?
faqs.answer: Storing 100 million unique search terms (average length 15 characters) with Top-5 suggestions at each node would consume ~25-30 GB of RAM. This easily fits inside a single modern server (e.g. 64GB RAM instance). To ensure fault tolerance and high throughput, the Trie is replicated across 10-20 read replicas behind a load balancer.

faqs.question: How are Trie shards partitioned to avoid uneven hotspots?
faqs.answer: Do not partition by the first letter (e.g. Shard A for 'a', Shard B for 'b') because letters like 's' or 'c' receive 20x more searches than 'z' or 'x'. Instead, partition by `hash(prefix) % num_shards` or use consistent hashing over the prefix string to distribute memory and query QPS uniformly across nodes.

faqs.question: How are breaking news and sudden viral trends accommodated if the Trie is rebuilt weekly?
faqs.answer: Use a hybrid architecture: (1) The Master Base Trie reflects rolling 7-day historical frequencies, and (2) A Real-Time Stream Tier (Redis Sorted Set) tracks queries trending over the past 30 minutes via Apache Flink. The API Gateway queries both and merges them, prioritizing sudden viral spikes.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Tries with Top-K pre-stored at nodes achieve O(prefix length) lookup time in under 2ms
Client debouncing (150-300ms) drops total server network requests by over 60%
Consistent hashing distributes prefix trees evenly across memory-mapped server clusters
Offline batch pipelines (Kafka + Spark) process billions of logs to refresh frequency weights
Hybrid streaming (Flink + Redis) injects breaking viral news without waiting for weekly re-indexes
data.takeaway: Search autocomplete systems deliver instant, sub-30ms responsiveness by combining in-memory prefix Tries with node-level Top-K caching, supported by asynchronous log aggregation pipelines.
